The '''2020–21 Clemson Tigers men's basketball team''' represented [[Clemson University]] during the [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Tigers were led by eleventh-year head coach [[Brad Brownell]] and played their home games at [[Littlejohn Coliseum]] in [[Clemson, South Carolina]] as members of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]].

The Tigers finished the season 16–8, and 10–6 in [[2020–21 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]] to finish in a tie for fifth place.  As the fifth seed in the [[2021 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]] they earned a bye into the Second Round where they lost to [[2020–21 Miami Hurricanes men's basketball team|Miami]].  They earned an at-large bid to the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as a seven seed in the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament#Midwest Regional|Midwest Region]].  They lost in the first round to 10 seed [[2020–21 Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball team|Rutgers]].

==Previous season==
The [[2019–20 Clemson Tigers men's basketball team|Tigers]] finished the [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2019–20 season]] 16–15, 9–11 in [[2019–20 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]] to finish in eighth place. The team was scheduled to play [[2019–20 Florida State Seminoles men's basketball team|Florida State]] in the quarterfinals of the [[2020 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]] before the tournament was cancelled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Statement from ACC on Men's Basketball Tournament |url=https://theacc.com/news/2020/3/12/statement-from-acc-on-mens-basketball-tournament.aspx |website=theacc.com |publisher=Atlantic Coast Conference |accessdate=12 March 2020}}</ref>  The [[2020 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] and [[2020 National Invitation Tournament|NIT]] were also cancelled due to the pandemic.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ncaa.org/about/resources/media-center/news/ncaa-cancels-remaining-winter-and-spring-championships|title=NCAA cancels remaining winter and spring championships|last=|first=|date=|website=|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200312202043/http://www.ncaa.org/about/resources/media-center/news/ncaa-cancels-remaining-winter-and-spring-championships |archive-date=2020-03-12 |access-date=}}</ref>
